newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola Enterprises sees higher expenses.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Enterprises sees higher expenses.

text.p: Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc said on Wednesday it expects increased expenses for stock-based compensation and benefits plans in the third quarter, compared its original 1996 expectations and 1995 third-quarter costs.

Based on the company's 70 percent year-to-date stock price rise, including a 32 percent third-quarter increase, Coca-Cola Enterprises said it will increase certain stock-related selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses, primarily non-cash amortization expense, by about $19 million, or $0.10 per share after tax, in the 1996 third quarter.
But it said it expects full-year 1996 comparable cash operating profit growth of 9.0 percent. It said this should translate into 20-25 percent comparable earnings per share growth.

Due to the company's evaluation of financial tools to mitigate stock-related expenses, and the significant cost already expensed for these programs, Coca-Cola Enterprises said it expects stock-based SG&A expenses will decline substantially in future periods.
